The radar cross section (RCS) of arbitrarily shaped bodies of revolution (BOR) can be computed by reducing the 3D scattering problem to a 1D problem using Fourier decomposition.
Surface Integral Equation (SIE) and Approximate Integral Equation (AIE) formulations are developed for homogeneous and composite dielectric and conducting BORs.
The method of moments is used to solve the coupled integral equations for unknown electric and magnetic surface currents.
The dielectric constant range considered is from 1.44 to 80, and conductivity range from 0 to 1000 mho/m.
The method accurately reproduces exact Mie series RCS results for dielectric spheres when matrix elements are computed precisely.
The AIE formulation incorporating the Leontovich impedance boundary condition requires solving only one current, reducing computational resources.
Seven Fourier modes (m = 0, ±1, ±2, ±3) are used for complex BORs like a human torso model under broadside plane wave incidence.
For long thin composite BORs, the zeroth-order Fourier mode alone can yield accurate surface currents and RCS.
The RCS of a human torso BOR model shows variation with incident angle and Fourier mode contributions.
Higher conductivity in composite BORs results in more resonances and higher RCS near backscattering directions.
The Mautz-Harrington combined field integral equation (CFIE) resolves non-uniqueness issues in EFIE solutions at interior resonances.
Surface currents are expanded using real triangular functions along the generating arc and Fourier series in the azimuthal angle.
The reciprocity theorem and measurement matrix concept are used to compute far scattered fields from surface currents.
The method can be extended to layered inhomogeneous BORs and varied-radius lossy dielectric cylinders.
Accurate RCS computations require about 10 expansion functions per free-space wavelength along the BOR generating arc.
The method applies to both axial and non-axial plane wave incidence.
The paper presents bistatic RCS results for composite metal-dielectric BORs with different incident angles.
The AIE approach yields the same surface currents and RCS as the SIE approach for highly lossy dielectric BORs.
The time dependence assumed in the formulation is exp(jωt).
The free-space intrinsic impedance used is approximately 120π ohms.
